observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher breaks down the Macedonian dance Crnogorka step by step from the back angle, demonstrating both parts individually and then combining them. She progressively increases the tempo and concludes with a full demonstration with music alongside other dancers.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces herself and the dance Crnogorka
Explains the region of origin, Skopsko Crnogora
Breaks down part one of the dance starting with the right leg
Breaks down part two of the dance
Combines part one and part two together slowly
Counts in full speed practice with 5-6-7-8
Demonstrates the dance with music alongside four dancers

steps_taught.name: Crnogorka Part 1
steps_taught.description: Step sequences moving side to side starting with right leg

steps_taught.name: Crnogorka Part 2
steps_taught.description: Crossing steps in front and behind

what_works: Clear verbal counts and repeated practice from the back view make it easy to follow along.
what_hinders: Only a single back-angle view is shown during the breakdown, lacking a mirrored front view.

quotes.text: In this Macedonian dance tutorial I'll be teaching a dance called Crnogorka.
There are two parts in this dance, starting with the first with the right.
Fantastic guys, let's see it together with the music.

extraction.distinctive_method: Teaching entirely from a rear-facing view so students can directly mimic footwork without mental inversion.
